name: OPA1655 / OPA1656 (single/dual CMOS FET-input, Burr-Brown audio)
tagline: TI's 2019 Burr-Brown FET-input audio op-amp: -129 dB THD+N at 20 kHz, fA-level current noise, 100 mA output; TI pitches it as the OPA2134/OPA2604 successor.
technology: CMOS FET-input. The datasheet says "FET-input architecture" and describes three gain stages with a feedforward path and a high-current rail-to-rail output stage. Supply is 4.5-36 V (±2.25 to ±18 V). The input common-mode range runs from V- to (V+) - 2.25 V, so the input is not rail-to-rail.

lineage.notes: SBOS901 was first issued as Advance Information in March 2019 and became production data (SBOS901A) in July 2019. The OPA1655 single was added in Rev B (Dec 2021), and its SOT-23-5 package went to production in Rev C (Sep 2022). No Rev D found as of Sep 2026. There is no second source.

reputation.summary: TI's own E2E FAQ presents the OPA1656 as the next-generation replacement for the OPA2134 and OPA2604 and calls it the lowest-voltage-noise high-voltage CMOS op-amp on the market (vendor claim). Hi-Fi and DIY users treat it as the modern, transparent, low-distortion FET-input Burr-Brown part. Community reports from the discovery sweep (not re-checked this run): in an ASR input-shorted phono noise test the roughly €5 OPA1656 matched the roughly €33 MUSES02; a Fosi ZA3 user said it 'basically wipes the floor' with Burson V7 Classic modules; Japanese listeners call it clean and balanced, with less colouration than the OPA2134; one SQ5J DAC test picked it for the I/V stage for a 'very modern' presentation; diyAudio and AMB threads discuss it as an OPA1612 substitute.
sonic_descriptors: low colouration and less harsh than OPA2134
OPA1655: high fidelity, smooth voices and instruments, slightly treble-leaning, good value (Japanese listening summary, low confidence)
typical_uses: headphone-amp gain and line stages (100 mA output; TI FAQ recommends it as a headphone driver)
MM phono preamps (datasheet application 8.2.1; fA-level current noise suits high source impedance)
op-amp rolling on SOIC-to-DIP8 adapters (Fosi and similar)
active tone controls and guitar/XLR interfaces (datasheet examples)
caveats: Packages are SOIC-8 only for the OPA1656 (SOIC-8 and SOT-23-5 for the OPA1655). There is no DIP, so rolling needs third-party adapter boards of variable quality and unknown origin.

It is fast (53 MHz GBW, 20 MHz unity-gain bandwidth), so socket and adapter parasitics and poor decoupling can cause ringing or oscillation. The datasheet rates capacitive load drive at 100 pF and shows RISO of 25-50 Ω taming overshoot. The oscillation risk in sockets is an engineering inference, not a documented incident.
The marketed 2.9 nV/rtHz is measured at 10 kHz. The datasheet gives 4.3 nV/rtHz at 1 kHz and 11.8 nV/rtHz at 100 Hz (CMOS 1/f noise), so bipolar parts are quieter in low-impedance circuits.
Maximum supply is 36 V (±18 V; absolute max 40 V), so it is not a drop-in for OPA2604 circuits running ±20-24 V rails.
The input is not rail-to-rail: VCM tops out at (V+) - 2.25 V, which limits follower headroom on low rails.
Iq is 3.9 mA per channel typical (4.6 mA max), about 7.8 mA per dual package.

counterfeit_notes: No vendor or forensic counterfeit report was found. A Sep 2026 web search returned a general summary that AliExpress OPA1656s may be fake or may not work, and that some sellers ship genuine parts in small orders and fakes in larger ones. That summary could not be tied to a specific OPA1656 thread; the related threads are diyAudio 'OPA1612 from Aliexpress, no counterfeit but why so cheap?' and the Super-Freq 'Fake op-amps' page. Treat it as low confidence. AliExpress listings such as 'New Original Non counterfeit OPA1656IDR' exist. Vendor-documented identifiers from the SBOS901C addendum: the OPA1656 exists only in SOIC-8 (D), marked 'OP1656' plus the TI logo and lot-trace code. The OPA1655 is marked 'OP1655' in SOIC and '2R8Q' in SOT-23-5. TI makes no DIP-8 package, so every DIP 'OPA1656' is a third-party adapter; inspect the SOIC on it. Suggested plausibility checks (engineering inference): about 7.8 mA supply current per dual package at ±15-18 V; pA-level input bias current, where a relabelled bipolar part would show nA or more; 20 MHz unity-gain bandwidth and 24 V/µs slew rate.
alternatives: OPA1612 (TI bipolar; 1.1 nV/rtHz, better with low source impedance, higher current noise)
OPA1652 / OPA1654 (older, cheaper TI FET-input SoundPlus, SBOS477; different die despite the 'OPA165x' name)
OPA1688 (named by TI, per discovery notes, as an OPA2604 replacement alongside the OPA1656)
MUSES02 (Nisshinbo; matched on noise in an ASR phono test)

The Advance Information (Mar 2019) specs may differ from production values; the Rev * PDF is needed to confirm.
PCNs (fab, assembly or test-site changes) for the OPA1655/OPA1656: none surfaced in a web search. The datasheet revision history shows no silicon change up to Rev C.
The JAJS document number and revision of the Japanese translation served at ti.com/jp/lit/ds/symlink/opa1656.pdf are unknown.
The datasheet does not explain the '.B' orderable variants (listed Active in the 9-Nov-2025 addendum) or the 'G4' suffix on OPA1656IDRG4. Confirm with TI that they are electrically identical.
The claim that 3e Audio A5/A7 ship the OPA1656 as the socketed default comes from a secondary GitHub summary (Frieve-A/audioreview), not a vendor page.
Community reputation claims (ASR MUSES02 comparison, Fosi ZA3, Japanese listening notes) were not re-checked this run because the 6-search budget was spent on vendor documents.
Naming collision: OPA1652/OPA1654 (SBOS477) are also titled 'OPA165x' but are a separate, older family; keep them out of this family.

revision_chain_notes:
TI SBOS901 (English), oldest to newest:
- Rev * (Advance Information, March 2019). Copy found: the existing chipdip URL https://static.chipdip.ru/lib/809/DOC005809868.pdf. Its search title begins 'ADVANCE INFORMATION Frequency (Hz) Voltage Noise Density', so the earlier label 'A or * (unconfirmed)' should become Rev *, medium confidence.
- Rev A (production data, July 2019). Copy found: the existing cimarrontechnology.com copy, uploaded 2021/06. It is titled 'OPA1656 Ultra-Low-Noise...' rather than the OPA165x title that came with Rev B, which supports Rev A. The existing unikeyic copy has the same title stem as the chipdip copy but without 'ADVANCE INFORMATION', so it may be Rev A (not confirmed).
- Rev B (December 2021, OPA1655 added, retitled OPA165x). New copy: RS docs.rs-online.com/d4ba/A700000009184805.pdf, medium confidence. The existing Mouser copy opa1656-1953342.pdf also came up for an exact 'SBOS901B' search and carries the OPA165x title, so it is probably Rev B too. The existing alldatasheet 1357767 copy is OPA165x, so Rev B or later.
- Rev C (September 2022, the current TI symlinks). New Rev B-or-later mirrors: DigiKey HTML datasheet and datasheet4u OPA1655/1535534. No Rev D was seen.

TI JAJSH26 (Japanese translation):
- JAJSH26C (March 2019, revised September 2022) is at ti.com/jp/lit/ds/symlink/opa1656.pdf.
- Missing: the JAJSH26 *, A and B letters. No copies were found.

Other vendors: none. TI/Burr-Brown is the sole source, so there are no Burr-Brown PDS, second-source or legacy-domain editions; the part postdates focus.ti.com.
